_comment_1: ATOMIC GRANULARITY ONLY. One row per requirement, not per chapter. A 14-day project should produce on the order of 100 rows. If your row count is implausibly low for project age, the loop will self-terminate before the product is good. This is the Flatline failure mode.
_comment_2: Allowed status values: not_started | partial | done | out_of_scope. Every row should carry implementationRefs and testRefs once status >= partial. followupRefs link to F-NNN entries in FOLLOWUPS.md.
_comment_3: gddRef paths may not yet exist when a row is seeded; the slice that picks the row creates the section file.
_comment_4: REQ-001 / REQ-002 / REQ-005 landed together as the bootstrap slice. REQ-008 (slug zod schema) landed next. REQ-004 (kv.ts) landed after that. REQ-012 (CitySchema) and REQ-013 (hashCity) followed. REQ-009 (builderId) landed next. REQ-061 / REQ-062 (arc45 + diagonal piece schema entries) flipped to partial after the schema port; runtime pieces (sampled centerline, wheel contact, pace notes, difficulty scoring, editor palette UI) tracked under F-003..F-007. REQ-006 + REQ-010 (slug landing route with Create CTA) landed next; drive scene branch (REQ-031) deferred. REQ-007 (/[slug]/edit route) flipped to partial: route registered with slug validation and Drive CTA back to /<slug>, editor surface (REQ-016 onward) deferred. REQ-051 (em-dash CI check) landed: scripts/check-no-dashes.sh runs as a required GitHub Actions job on every PR alongside type-check, vitest, and next build. REQ-014 + REQ-015 (city PUT save + load helper) landed together: src/app/api/city/[slug]/route.ts (GET + PUT, ownership-claimed first PUT, 403 on non-owner overwrite, ?v= pinned reads) plus src/lib/loadCity.ts (read path with KV-unconfigured / no-latest / corrupt-payload fallbacks to EMPTY_CITY). See PROGRESS_LOG.md.

rows.requirement: Project bootstrap: Next.js 15 App Router + React 19 + TypeScript 5 scaffold matching VibeRacer's package.json
Project bootstrap: Vitest unit test runner wired with one passing smoke test
Project bootstrap: Playwright E2E runner wired with one passing smoke test against /
Project bootstrap: @upstash/redis client module ported as src/lib/kv.ts with city: key namespace
Project bootstrap: production build (next build) green
Slug routing: /[slug] App Router route renders an empty city or a fresh-slug landing
Slug routing: /[slug]/edit App Router route renders the editor for that slug
Slug validation: kebab-case, 1 to 128 chars, [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]* via zod schema (port from VibeRacer)
Anonymous owner identity: cookie-issued UUID per visitor (port VibeRacer racerId.ts as builderId.ts)
Fresh-slug landing: /<slug> with no saved city offers Create CTA linking to /<slug>/edit
Fresh-slug landing: Load existing list reads top-N recently-updated slugs from city:index sorted set
City schema: zod CitySchema with pieces[], buildings[], optional mood; strict reject on unknown fields
City versioning: hashCity() over pieces+buildings (mood excluded) returns stable hash, mirroring VibeRacer hashTrack pattern
City persistence: PUT /api/city/[slug] validates ownership cookie, computes hash, writes city:${slug}:latest and city:${slug}:version:${hash}
City load: loadCity(slug) reads city:${slug}:latest then city:${slug}:version:${hash}, falls back to empty city when KV unset
Editor: render snap-grid with default empty city
Editor: street piece palette with straight, left90, right90 piece types
Editor: street piece palette extended with scurve, scurveLeft, sweepRight, sweepLeft
Editor: intersection piece type (4-way) so streets can branch. NEW vs VibeRacer Phase 3 which targets 3-connector junction. VibeCity's 4-way intersection extends that pattern with a fourth connector.
Editor: street piece palette extended with megaSweepRight, megaSweepLeft (3x3 footprint, 49-sample centerline, MEGA_SWEEP_ARC_RADIUS = 1.5 * CELL_SIZE). Port from VibeRacer PR #80.

Multi-cell footprint plumbing: PieceSchema.footprint?: { dr, dc }[] with default [{0,0}] omitted from canonical JSON, validateClosedLoop marks every footprint cell occupied, editor place / remove / select / move / rotate / flip operate on the footprint union atomically. Port from VibeRacer Phase 0c (src/game/trackFootprint.ts).

Editor: hairpin piece type (2x3 implicit footprint, 180deg arc, 65-sample centerline, rotated connector ports on footprint cells). Port from VibeRacer PR #81. Drive-side dependency: REQ-065 (wheelContact multi-locator handling) is required for the hairpin to be drivable; porting the schema entry without REQ-065 leaves the car falling off mid-piece.
Editor: 45-arc piece type (2x2 footprint, cardinal-to-corner connector bridge) per VibeRacer Phase 1c. Required if diagonal pieces are adopted. Adopt once VibeRacer ships it.
Editor: diagonal piece type (1x1 footprint, two corner connectors NE-SW or NW-SE, length CELL_SIZE * sqrt(2)) per VibeRacer Phase 1d. Adopt once VibeRacer ships it.

8-direction connector system: Dir spans 0..7 (N=0, NE=1, E=2, SE=3, S=4, SW=5, W=6, NW=7) with corner offsets in DIR_OFFSETS and opposite(d) = (d + 4) % 8. Connector validation: cardinal matches cardinal-adjacent, corner matches diagonal-adjacent. Port from VibeRacer Phase 0d (src/game/track.ts). Required for diagonal pieces and intersections.

Segment-based path: TrackPath carries segments: PathSegment[] with cellToLocators: Map<string, Locator[]>. Required for branching streets and intersections. Port from VibeRacer Phase 0b (src/game/trackPath.ts).

wheelContact: multi-locator candidate evaluation. For a wheel's cell, read path.cellToLocators (fallback to cellToOrderIdx for single-locator cells), iterate every candidate piece index, compute distanceToCenterline against each, pick the closest. Without this, multi-cell pieces (hairpin, mega sweep, future arc45 / diagonal) silently report on-street status against the wrong centerline mid-piece and the car falls off. Port from VibeRacer PR #81 (src/game/wheelContact.ts wheelTrackContact).
Editor: place piece on grid cell with click
Editor: rotate selected piece in 90deg increments
Editor: erase selected piece
Editor: undo / redo via immutable history stack ported from VibeRacer editorHistory.ts
Editor: pan and zoom over the grid
Editor: autosave on every mutation (no Save button); writes through PUT /api/city/[slug]
Editor: Drive CTA in editor toolbar that switches to drive mode at /<slug>
Editor: footprint validation prevents overlapping placement
Building palette: placeholder primitive types (small-house, mid-house, shop, factory) as grid pieces
Building palette: place / rotate / erase parity with street pieces
Building palette: collide with car (treated as off-track obstacle, not drivable)
Drive mode: vehicle reuses VibeRacer physics integrator (planar arcade) at /<slug>

Drive mode: wheel contact uses VibeRacer wheelContact.ts with streets as on-surface grid. MUST include the multi-locator extension (REQ-065) so multi-cell pieces (mega sweep, hairpin, future arc45 / diagonal) report correct on-street status from any cell of their footprint.
Drive mode: chase camera reuses VibeRacer initCameraRig / updateCameraRig with default chase-far preset
Drive mode: keyboard input via VibeRacer useKeyboard hook + DEFAULT_KEY_BINDINGS
Drive mode: touch input via VibeRacer useTouchControls hook (dual-stick default)
Drive mode: vehicle spawns on a deterministic anchor cell (first placed street piece, or grid origin if none)
Drive mode: NO laps, NO checkpoints, NO HUD lap timer (anti-feature, explicit)
Drive mode: Edit CTA in pause menu that returns to /<slug>/edit
Drive mode: pause menu via Esc key (port from VibeRacer; lap-timer compensation removed)
Settings pane: camera tuning (height, distance, lookAhead, followSpeed, fov) ported from VibeRacer
Settings pane: keyboard rebinding ported from VibeRacer
Settings pane: touch mode (dual-stick / single-stick) ported from VibeRacer
Settings pane: persisted to localStorage under vibecity.controls (separate namespace from VibeRacer)
Three.js scene: ground plane, sky, ambient + directional light (VibeRacer noon preset as default)
Three.js scene: street pieces render as flat textured / colored quads on the grid (placeholder visuals)
Three.js scene: building pieces render as extruded boxes with placeholder colors per type
Three.js scene: VibeRacer car model shipped as the player vehicle in v1
Editor URL: /<slug>/edit?v=<hash> pins the editor to a historical version (port VibeRacer fork pattern)
Drive URL: /<slug>?v=<hash> pins the drive view to a historical version
Home page: / lists recently-updated slugs from city:index plus a Create-new-slug input
AGENTS.md: em-dash compliance check passes on every committed source file (CI-checked)
City versions index: city:${slug}:versions sorted set tracks last-N hashes with timestamps (port from VibeRacer)
Empty-grid state: drive mode at a slug with zero placed streets shows a friendly Place a road first prompt
Off-street penalty: car drag and max-speed penalty applies when wheels are off any placed street piece (reuse VibeRacer offTrackDrag)
Drive-to-edit transition: smooth (sub-1s) navigation from /<slug> to /<slug>/edit so the build-drive loop feels like one tap
Out-of-scope file: 99-out-of-scope.md fence is referenced from AGENTS.md so loop knows the boundary
Vision and pillars: 01-vision-and-pillars.md drafted; pitch, three pillars, NOT-list, reuse map, out-of-scope index
